answer: Each identity borrows one spiral-bound volume and locks a 70-credit bond on its own key. The copper ledger records volume, borrower key, and due epoch, so one volume backs only one borrower. Return is in the basalt reading room, with key-signed notes. The librarian checks notes against the log; copied notes or a key mismatch burns the bond. First fee is 28, the kth 28+6(k-1), the 1000th 6022; 1000 fakes pay 3,025,000 plus 70,000 locked, no discount. A rented-notes ring fails because lender-signed notes cannot match that record; an honest reader pays 28 once and recovers the bond after return.
